candidates.rationale: Built for this site during the homepage migration. Logo row, navy bar, hamburger and separators all already match. The boilerplate decorate() already tags any <li> containing a <ul> as .nav-drop, so nested markup is understood.
gaps: No active-trail detection. The source expands the submenu of the section the current page belongs to; a shared /nav document cannot know that at author time, so the block must derive it from window.location.pathname at runtime.
The existing CSS renders a nested <ul> as an absolutely-positioned click dropdown. The source renders it as a static second row below the navy bar, always visible for the active section only.

candidates.rationale: Generic dropdown nav. Would discard the brand styling already built for this site.

content_model.row_contract: /nav document, three sections: brand | sections | tools. Second level is a nested <ul> inside the parent <li>.
content_model.note: Header is document-driven in this repo, not a block model — there is no _header.json and none is needed. The authoring change is to the /nav document: the Agents/Brokers and Policyholders items each gain a nested <ul>.

behavior_contract.notes: The source submenu is server-rendered for the active trail, not a dropdown — no hover or click behaviour to reproduce. The active trail must be computed client-side. Keep the boilerplate's existing keyboard/escape handling for the mobile hamburger.

candidates.rationale: The `panel` variant was built for this exact component during the homepage migration. hero.js already tags rows as .hero-image / .hero-panel and the CSS matches the measured geometry.
gaps: blocks/hero/_hero.json declares only image / imageAlt / text and has no `classes` field, so the `panel` variant cannot be selected in Universal Editor. The CSS variant exists and is unreachable to authors.

content_model.row_contract: row 1 = panel (prompt paragraph + list of CTA links), row 2 = banner image. hero.js tags whichever row contains a picture/img as .hero-image and the other as .hero-panel.

behavior_contract.notes: Static. The CTA links are ordinary anchors.

content_model.note: Drawn by the hero block's border-image, a decision carried over from the homepage migration. Deliberately not a block, so authors cannot place an empty rule.

candidates.rationale: Byte-identical markup and measurements to the homepage footer this block was built from. No gaps.

content_model.row_contract: /footer document: a paragraph of pipe-separated links, then a copyright paragraph.
content_model.note: Document-driven like the header; no model partial.
